label: Hired mercenaries
summary: The list of hired mercenaries, for the military window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list. A part of the window is shown when this list or the hired holy orders list is not empty.

label: Knights
summary: The list of knights, used as the data source of the knights window and the accolade window.
details: Vanilla also counts its entries to show the number of knights.

label: Levy upkeep in goods
summary: The monthly upkeep of the raised levies, paid in barter goods.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the barter goods icon and, in the tooltip, as an amount per month. It is a number with decimals.

label: Levy upkeep in gold
summary: The monthly upkeep of the raised levies, paid in gold.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the gold icon and, in the tooltip, as an amount per month. It is a number with decimals.

label: Levy upkeep from treasury
summary: The monthly upkeep of the raised levies, paid from the treasury.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the treasury icon and, in the tooltip, as an amount per month. It is a number with decimals.

label: Men-at-arms count text
summary: A ready-made text with the number of men-at-arms and their cap, going by its name.
details: The military window shows it as a plain label. The exact format of the text comes from the game's code.

label: Men-at-arms count tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the men-at-arms count and cap, going by its name.
details: The military window uses it as the tooltip of a part.

label: Maintenance
summary: A number with decimals that, going by its name, is the upkeep of the military.
details: Vanilla does not use it in any text or GUI file, so what exactly it adds up is not shown.

label: Military item
summary: The military item of the military view, passed on as the data context of parts of the military window.
details: Vanilla uses it only to set the data context of parts of the military window.

label: Reinforcement cost tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the cost of military reinforcement, going by its name.
details: The military window uses it as a tooltip in two places.

label: Raised levies
summary: How many levies are currently raised.
details: Vanilla uses it in the three levy upkeep tooltips, shown as a whole number on the line below the upkeep per month.

label: Piety military expenses
summary: The military costs that are paid in piety, handed on as a context for the parts that show them.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the data context of two parts of the military window. It also appears in a check that compares the gold, treasury, prestige, piety and barter goods expenses with zero: when all are zero, the window shows a 'nothing' text.

label: Prestige military expenses
summary: The military costs that are paid in prestige, handed on as a context for the parts that show them.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the data context of two parts of the military window. It also appears in a check that compares the gold, treasury, prestige, piety and barter goods expenses with zero: when all are zero, the window shows a 'nothing' text.

label: Rally point number info
summary: A text about the number of rally points.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Rally points
summary: The list of rally points, used as the data source of lists in the military window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of two lists in the military window.

label: Admin realm power text
summary: A ready-made text with the total power of the admin realm, going by its name.
details: The military window shows it as a label. The game documents nothing more.

label: Admin realm strength text
summary: A ready-made text with the total strength of the admin realm, going by its name.
details: The military window shows it as a label. The game documents nothing more.

label: Treasury military expenses
summary: The military costs that are paid from the treasury, handed on as a context for the parts that show them.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the data context of two parts of the military window. It also appears in a check that compares the gold, treasury, prestige, piety and barter goods expenses with zero: when all are zero, the window shows a 'nothing' text.

label: Has all barter goods expenses
summary: Going by its name, whether all the raised military expenses are in barter goods.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the military window (once).

label: Has all gold expenses
summary: Going by its name, whether all the raised military expenses are in gold.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the military window (3 times).

label: Has all piety expenses
summary: Going by its name, whether all the raised military expenses are in piety.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the military window (2 times).

label: Has all prestige expenses
summary: Going by its name, whether all the raised military expenses are in prestige.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the military window (2 times).

label: Has all treasury expenses
summary: Going by its name, whether all the raised military expenses are in treasury.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the military window (3 times).

label: Has any military expenses
summary: Going by its name, whether there are any raised military expenses.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the military window (twice).

label: Has embarked armies
summary: Going by its name, whether there are embarked armies.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the military window (twice).

label: Is admin title with troops
summary: Going by its name, whether the given title is an admin title with troops.
details: Vanilla passes the title of the current row. It combines this with a check on requesting the title's army, to decide what the row shows.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a title from the GUI, such as Title.Self

label: Is automating armies
summary: Whether army automation is turned on.
details: Vanilla uses it with Not to switch a control off while automation runs.

label: Controls other titles' troops
summary: Going by its name, whether the troops of other titles are being controlled.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Reinforcements enabled
summary: Whether military reinforcements are switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the reinforcement toggle in the military window.

label: Is tab active
summary: Whether the named tab of the military window is the one currently shown.
details: Vanilla uses the tab names 'owned_armies', 'title_troops' and 'mercenary' to show the matching page.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'owned_armies', 'title_troops' or 'mercenary'

label: Add rally point
summary: Going by its name, adds a rally point; used on a button click.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on two clicks in the military window.

label: Reinforcement click
summary: Going by its name, reacts to a click in the reinforcement part.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on two clicks in the military window.

label: Return controlled men-at-arms
summary: Going by its name, returns controlled men-at-arms; used on a button click.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on two clicks. The input does not say what 'controlled' means.

label: Return reassigned men-at-arms
summary: Going by its name, returns reassigned men-at-arms; used on a button click.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on two clicks. The input does not say to whom they were reassigned.

label: Military view
summary: The military view itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses the same name `Self` on many types for this. Here vanilla gives no example for this type.

label: Set active tab
summary: Switches the military window to the named tab.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla uses the names 'owned_armies', 'title_troops' and 'mercenary' on the tab buttons.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'owned_armies', 'title_troops' or 'mercenary'

label: Allow knight
summary: Lets a knight join armies only if their prowess is among the highest in the realm (the default).
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the Allow button of the knights window and from buttons of the accolade window, next to the Force and Forbid ones.

label: Forbid knight
summary: Forbids a knight from ever joining armies as a knight.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the Forbid button of the knights window and from buttons of the accolade window. Its tooltip says this keeps the character safe from dying in battle.

label: Force knight
summary: Makes a knight always join armies, whatever their prowess.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the Force button of the knights window and from buttons of the accolade window. Its tooltip says the knight may take the place of one with higher prowess.

label: Show automation options
summary: Going by its name, shows the options for army automation; used on a button click.
details: Returns nothing.

label: Show knights
summary: Going by its name, shows the knights; used on a button click.
details: Returns nothing. Going by its name.

label: Show levies
summary: Going by its name, shows the levies; used on a button click.
details: Returns nothing. Going by its name.

label: Levies use barter goods
summary: Whether the levies are paid for in barter goods.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick which upkeep display to show: barter goods, treasury, or gold when neither applies.

label: Levies use treasury
summary: Whether the levies are paid for from the treasury.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick which upkeep display to show: treasury, barter goods, or gold when neither applies.

label: Event troop itself
summary: The event troop row itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Going by its name; vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Can be raised
summary: Whether this event troop can be raised.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the military window.

label: Associated war
summary: The war associated with this event troop, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the data context of a part of the military window.

label: Troop composition
summary: The makeup of this event troop, handed on as a context for the parts that show it.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the data context of a part of the military window. Going by its name, it describes what kinds of soldiers the troop has.

label: Troop name
summary: The name of this event troop.
details: Vanilla shows it as a label and in the tooltip that says what raising the troop does.

label: Raisable regiments
summary: How many regiments of this event troop can be raised.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it. It is a whole number.

label: Raisable soldiers
summary: How many soldiers can be raised from this event troop.
details: Vanilla uses it in the raise tooltip, after the text about a new army. It is a whole number.

label: Raise province name
summary: The name of the province where this event troop would be raised.
details: Vanilla uses it in the raise tooltip. The input does not say more.

label: Troop regiments
summary: The list of regiments of this event troop.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list, and checks whether it is empty to show an empty-state part.

label: Is inheritable
summary: Whether this event troop is passed on to the heir.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it, and its opposite, to switch between two display parts.

label: Event troop
summary: This event troop, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the function that raises event troops, when the player clicks the raise button.

label: Brush mode itself
summary: The mix brush mode itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: A tool of the game's internal GUI. Vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Is mix brush active
summary: Whether the mix brush is the active tool of the engine's map editor.
details: Vanilla shows it as the pressed state of the toolbar button 'Mix Brush'.

label: Brush mode
summary: This mix brush mode, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `Self` on many types for this; there is no example for this type.

label: Modifier itself
summary: This modifier entry itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Modifier icon
summary: The icon of this modifier.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an image in the character window and in shared GUI parts.

label: Modifier name
summary: The name of this modifier.
details: Going by its name; the same function exists on many types. Vanilla has no example for this type.

label: Modifier preview list
summary: The preview list of this modifier (the game's timed modifier preview list).
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the character window and of shared GUI parts.

label: Scaled modifier tooltip data
summary: The data for a tooltip showing one modifier effect, scaled.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a tooltip part. What the scaling does is not shown in the input.

label: Modifier tooltip data
summary: The data for a tooltip showing one modifier effect.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the character window and of shared GUI parts.

label: Static modifier
summary: The static modifier behind this entry.
details: Vanilla reads the name from it for a label, and uses it as a data context.

label: Has tooltip data
summary: Whether this modifier has tooltip data of the given kind.
details: Vanilla asks with 'single_modifier', 'preview_list' and 'scaled_single_modifier' to show or hide parts of the character window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted tag, such as 'single_modifier', 'preview_list' or 'scaled_single_modifier'

label: Modifier
summary: This modifier entry, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `Self` on many types for this; there is no example for this type.

label: Obligation checkboxes
summary: The list of obligation levels shown as checkboxes in the window for changing a vassal contract.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list.

label: Obligation line trees
summary: The list of obligation levels shown as a line tree in the window for changing a vassal contract.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list.

label: Obligation radio buttons
summary: The list of obligation levels shown as radio buttons in the window for changing a vassal contract.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list.

label: Contract window itself
summary: The contract change window itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Close
summary: Closes the window for changing a vassal contract.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a button click.

label: Confirmation window
summary: The confirmation window of the interaction, handed on as a context for the parts inside it.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the data context of a part of the contract window.

label: Contract preview
summary: The contract as it would be after the chosen changes.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and asks it whether it is a tributary contract, and whether obligations should be shown.

label: Preview goods breakdown
summary: The breakdown of where the previewed contract's barter goods amount comes from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a breakdown part.

label: Preview barter goods
summary: The barter goods amount of the previewed contract.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a label, with the format suffix |=2.

label: Preview herd
summary: The herd amount of the previewed contract.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a label, with the format suffix |=1.

label: Preview levies
summary: The number of levies of the previewed contract.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it; it shows the formatted version instead. It is a whole number.

label: Preview levies text
summary: The levies of the previewed contract as a ready-made text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a label.

label: Preview piety
summary: The piety amount of the previewed contract.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a label, with the format suffix |=2.

label: Preview prestige
summary: The prestige amount of the previewed contract.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a label, with the format suffix |=2.

label: Preview tax
summary: The tax amount of the previewed contract.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a label, with the format suffix |=2.

label: Preview herd breakdown
summary: The breakdown of where the previewed contract's herd amount comes from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a breakdown part.

label: Preview levies breakdown
summary: The breakdown of where the previewed contract's levies come from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a breakdown part.

label: Preview opinion breakdown
summary: The breakdown of opinion for the previewed contract.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a breakdown part. Going by its name, it explains the opinion effect of the changes.

label: Preview piety breakdown
summary: The breakdown of where the previewed contract's piety amount comes from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a breakdown part.

label: Preview prestige breakdown
summary: The breakdown of where the previewed contract's prestige amount comes from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a breakdown part.

label: Preview tax breakdown
summary: The breakdown of where the previewed contract's tax amount comes from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a breakdown part.

label: Obligation level description
summary: The description text of the obligation level.
details: Vanilla shows it as a label in the contract window.

label: Obligation level tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for one obligation level option.
details: Vanilla passes the option of the current row.

label: Has barter goods obligations
summary: Whether the previewed contract has obligations paid in barter goods.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the contract window.

label: Has herd obligations
summary: Whether the previewed contract has herd obligations.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the contract window.

label: Has levy obligations
summary: Whether the previewed contract has levy obligations.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the contract window.

label: Has piety obligations
summary: Whether the previewed contract has piety obligations.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the contract window.

label: Has prestige obligations
summary: Whether the previewed contract has prestige obligations.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of a part of the contract window.

label: Has tax obligations
summary: Whether the previewed contract has tax obligations.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the tax row, together with a check that the liege's government has no treasury.

label: Is current obligation level
summary: Whether the given obligation level option is the one the contract has now.
details: Vanilla passes the option of the current list item and uses it as a visible condition (twice).

label: Is level enabled
summary: Whether the given obligation level option can be picked.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of an option's control.

label: Is level selected
summary: Whether the given obligation level option is the one chosen in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it for the pressed state of the option and, with Not, to hide parts of it.

label: Is level visible
summary: Whether the given obligation level option is shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible state of an option.

label: Preview same as current
summary: Whether the previewed contract is the same as the current one.
details: Vanilla uses it with Not as the enabled condition of a control, so the control is enabled only when the preview differs from the current contract.

label: Is rightful liege
summary: Going by its name, whether the liege in this contract is the rightful liege.
details: Vanilla shows a part of the window only when neither this nor the previewed contract's tributary check is true.

label: Reset to current
summary: Going by its name, resets the previewed contract to the current one; used on a button click.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a button click.

label: Select obligation level
summary: Chooses the given obligation level option in the window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on the click of an option.

label: Contract window
summary: The contract change window, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `Self` on many types for this; there is no example for this type.

label: Send
summary: Going by its name, sends the changed contract; used on a button click.
details: Returns nothing.

label: Option itself
summary: This obligation level option itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Option icon
summary: The icon of this obligation level option.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an image.

label: Option name
summary: The name of this obligation level option.
details: Vanilla shows it as a label.

label: Obligation level option
summary: This obligation level option, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the window's functions that check or select a level, and to a line tree that places the option.

label: Move window itself
summary: The window for moving the domicile, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Close
summary: Closes the window for moving the domicile.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a button click.

label: Move window
summary: The window for moving the domicile, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `Self` on many types for this; there is no example for this type.

label: Move tool itself
summary: The move tool itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: A tool of the game's internal GUI. Vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Move tool
summary: The move tool, to pass on to other functions.
details: A tool of the game's internal GUI. Vanilla uses `Self` on many types for this; there is no example for this type.

label: Bookmark itself
summary: This multiplayer bookmark entry itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Bookmark date
summary: The date of this bookmark.
details: Vanilla asks it for its long text form and shows that as a label in the multiplayer setup.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this bookmark is the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a part in the multiplayer setup.

label: Select
summary: Selects this bookmark.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a click in the multiplayer setup.

label: Bookmark
summary: This multiplayer bookmark entry, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `Self` on many types for this; there is no example for this type.

label: Multiplayer config
summary: The multiplayer settings, in a form the buttons can change.
details: Vanilla calls functions on it from button clicks: the ones that set the game offline, private or public.

label: Setup window itself
summary: The multiplayer setup window itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Can host
summary: Whether a multiplayer game can be hosted now.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of the host button.

label: Cancel
summary: Cancels the multiplayer setup.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a button click.

label: Default server name
summary: The server name the setup suggests.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a field.

label: Default server password
summary: The server password the setup suggests.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a field.

label: Multiplayer config
summary: The multiplayer settings, for reading.
details: Vanilla reads from it whether the game is offline and the tooltip text for private games.

label: Host
summary: Starts hosting the multiplayer game.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when Return is pressed in the setup fields, and from buttons.

label: Host tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the host button.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip.

label: Setup window
summary: The multiplayer setup window, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `Self` on many types for this; there is no example for this type.

label: Show multiplayer config
summary: Whether the multiplayer settings should be shown.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Music categories
summary: The list of music categories of the music player.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list, and checks whether it is empty.

label: Music player itself
summary: The music player itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses `AccessSelf` on many types and gives no example for this one.

label: Tracks of category
summary: The list of tracks in the music category that is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list, and checks whether it is empty.

label: Category on/off text
summary: The text of the button that switches the given music category on or off in the engine's music player.
details: Vanilla shows it on the small button inside each category's button; clicking it toggles whether the category is enabled. The exact words are not in the GUI file.

label: Category name
summary: The name of the given music category, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it on each category's button in the engine's music player; clicking the button selects the category.

label: Music density
summary: The music density setting as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a slider. It is a decimal number.

label: Music density text
summary: The music density setting as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the whole text of the game's entry for the density value.

label: Playback status
summary: A whole number for the music player's playback status.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of the play/pause button, in the music player and its mini controller. Going by its name, it picks the frame (picture) for playing or paused; which number means what is not shown.

label: Elapsed time
summary: How much of the playing track has been played, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a label.

label: Playing track name
summary: The name of the track that is playing.
details: Vanilla shows it as a label.

label: Selected category
summary: The music category that is selected.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Track on/off text
summary: The text of the button that switches the given track on or off in the engine's music player.
details: Vanilla shows it on the small button inside each track's row; clicking it toggles whether the track is enabled. The exact words are not in the GUI file.

label: Track name
summary: The name of the given music track, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it on each track's row in the engine's music player, for the tracks of the selected category.

label: Track text color
summary: The text color to use for the given track in the list.
details: Vanilla passes the track of the current row and uses the result as the font color. It is a color with four parts.

label: Volume
summary: The music volume as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a slider.

label: Volume text
summary: The music volume as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the whole text of the game's entry for the volume value.

label: Has selected category
summary: Whether a music category is selected.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Is playing
summary: Whether the music player is playing.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its opposite, to switch between the play and pause parts.

label: Playing track selectable
summary: Whether the track that is playing can be selected in the list.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part of the music player. Going by its name, it concerns the playing track.
